text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Investors are poised for a showdown with the Nigerian stock exchange over the recently-introduced central clearing system which they say does not give them share certificates as physical evidence of their investments.
- Commissioning of Nigeria's aluminium plant scheduled for this month has been postponed again following the ability of the project managers to achieve 100 percent completion.
- A new board of directors for Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas Company Limited is likely to be constituted next month.
- Amid deeping energy crisis in Nigeria, the government has cleared all formalities for the take-off of the $1.5 billion private export-oriented proposed Brass Refineries.
- Oil minister Dan Etete may not attend this week's Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) biannual ministerial meeting in Vienna, Austria.
- Ten thousand metric tonnes of fuel arrive in Lagos at the weekend, enough to last only three days.
- No fewer than 10 major companies have served notice of temporary suspension of operations due to the persisting fuel scarcity.
- Nigerian students have given the federal government a 48-hour ultimatum to find a solution to the lingering fuel supply crisis in the country or face nationwide demonstration.
